questions.question: Why does the chapter prefer least squares to drawing a line by eye?
questions.answer: Least squares provides a reproducible fitting rule: analysts who agree on the data and method agree on the fitted line, unlike eyeball approximations.

questions.question: What does Kenosha teach about deleting unusual observations?
questions.answer: Removing Kenosha improves fit measures, but an unusual point can contain meaningful information; the goal is to understand its effect rather than automatically omit it.
